```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

treatledger turns a table of treatment records into the cumulative exposures
used in late-effects research on childhood cancer survivors. It is a research
tool and does not give care recommendations.

```{r setup}
library(treatledger)
```

## 1. Prepare your data

Use one row per treatment course. The columns can have any names; tell the
functions which is which. The demonstration cohort is invented.

```{r}
treatledger_demo
```

Doses of drugs should be cumulative and in mg/m². Radiotherapy doses can be
in Gy or cGy, with the treated region in its own column.

## 2. Choose a factor set

The anthracycline factor sets disagree, so treatledger makes you choose one
and records it in every result.

```{r}
tl_factor_sets()
anthracycline_factors[, c("set", "agent", "factor", "note")]
```

## 3. Calculate exposures

```{r}
tl_dox_equivalent(treatledger_demo, set = "cog_v6")
tl_ced(treatledger_demo)
tl_radiation(treatledger_demo)
```

Or all at once:

```{r}
tl_summarise(treatledger_demo, anthracycline_set = "cog_v6")
```

## 4. Check how much the factor set matters

Running the same cohort under both anthracycline sets is a simple sensitivity
analysis.

```{r}
cog <- tl_dox_equivalent(treatledger_demo, set = "cog_v6")
fei <- tl_dox_equivalent(treatledger_demo, set = "feijen2019")
data.frame(patient_id = cog$patient_id,
           cog_v6 = cog$dox_equivalent_mg_m2,
           feijen2019 = fei$dox_equivalent_mg_m2)
```

## 5. Read the flags

The `flags` column reports anything you should check: doses converted from
mg/kg, missing doses, unrecognised units and radiotherapy with no region. A
patient with a missing dose gets `NA` rather than a partial total.

## Reporting

When you publish results, state the treatledger version and the factor sets
used, for example: "Cumulative exposures were calculated with treatledger
0.1.0 using the COG v6.0 anthracycline factors and the cyclophosphamide
equivalent dose of Green et al. (2014)."
